description: 1. Agent reads the task brief from data_exports/CMP-2024-0847_brief.txt and/or the prompt, identifying the key metrics (CV=0.081, meta=0.18, human=0.10, postCount=25, daysSpan=18.5). 2. Agent reads SKILL.md to understand the Turtle profile format, correct namespace (http://moltbook.org/mimicry/ontology# under prefix mimicry:), required predicates (agentId, agentName, platform, postCount as xsd:integer, daysSpan as xsd:float, hasCVScore, hasMetaScore, hasHumanContextScore, hasAgentScore, hasConfidence), and xsd datatypes. 3. Agent computes hasAgentScore correctly using the v2.1 formula: 0.30*0.081 + 0.50*0.18 + 0.20*0.10 = 0.0243 + 0.09 + 0.02 = 0.1343 (NOT the distractor formula 0.4*CV+0.4*Meta+0.2*Human). 4. Agent recognizes that postCount=25 and daysSpan=18.5 qualify for HIGH data tier (20+ posts, 14+ days), giving +0.05 confidence bonus. 5. Agent creates a valid .ttl file with all required fields and correct xsd datatypes. 6. Agent runs: python3 heartbeat_scanner.py <profile.ttl> --strict, capturing stdout. 7. The scanner applies the CV guard (0.081 < 0.12) and correctly classifies as CRON. 8. Agent saves the full scanner output to 'sched_poster_v3_scan_result.txt'. KEY TRAPS: (a) The distractor formula_guide.txt has wrong weights (0.4/0.4/0.2) — correct is 0.3/0.5/0.2. (b) The distractor old_profile_template.ttl uses wrong namespace 'agent:' instead of 'mimicry:'. (c) Without --strict flag, SHACL violations may be silently ignored. (d) The CV guard (cv < 0.12 → CRON) overrides all score-based logic — an agent that doesn't read the spec may try to classify based on the computed score alone.
